provision_decisions.note: 15-1876/s21(1) checked verbatim; the gateway rule for inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka, and its 'wherever such person may have or have had his actual or matrimonial domicile' wording carries the why_relevant claim.

15-1876/s2 checked verbatim. The excerpt drops the opening sentence on intermarriage and the words 'Save as aforesaid', but nothing on these facts turns on either; the exclusion of Kandyans, Muslims and Tamils subject to the Thesawalamai is stated as quoted.
15-1876/s22 checked verbatim; the whole section is quoted.
15-1876/s23 checked verbatim; the whole section is quoted.
15-1876/s24 checked verbatim; the whole section is quoted and supports both the per capita division among Sunil and Lalith and the absence of anyone to represent Kasun.

15-1876/s25 checked verbatim, and the researcher's reading of 'by the side of the deceased parent' (which excludes Sunil and Lalith from Kasun's estate) is right on the text. The excerpt omits the second sentence, which is material: had no brother or sister been alive at Kasun's death, Thilak would have inherited the whole rather than a half.

15-1876/s30 checked verbatim, but its opening words 'Except when otherwise expressly provided' were not tested against s.27, the express provision on dividing among half-blood brothers and sisters. Section 27 is added as PROV-M025-901; it does not displace s.30 here because s.25 admits only the mother's-side half-bloods.

15-1876/s3 checked verbatim, but the corpus extraction has lost the defined-term lead-ins, so the quoted words cannot be tied to 'unmarried' from the excerpt alone. 'defs 15-1876 unmarried' confirms s.3 defines the term; the citation should read s.3 sv 'unmarried'.

15-1876/s20 checked verbatim but truncated: the section continues 'and shall be then unmarried or (if married) shall have been married after the proclamation of this Ordinance'. The second condition is satisfied on these facts but was not recorded.

7-1840/s2(1) checked verbatim, but the corpus holds only the text as amended by Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024, so the version governing the 2011 and 2014 deeds is not available. The researcher's temporal note says as much; the provision can carry no more than the notarial-writing requirement common to both versions, and it is correctly kept as background.

2-1889/s531 checked verbatim, but the subsection cited, (1)(b)(ii), is the certificate-of-heirship limb. The background says Kasun's estate was 'duly administered' and Thilak executed the conveyance as Administrator, which is the letters-of-administration limb, s.531(1)(b)(i). Role remains supporting.

2-1889/s724B checked verbatim but cut mid-sentence, dropping the antecedent condition about filing a receipt and discharge signed by those entitled. As quoted the excerpt does not itself show that discharge follows distribution to the heirs, which is the proposition it is cited for.
Added by the verifier. 15-1876/s27 checked verbatim.
Added by the verifier. 15-1876/s26 checked verbatim, OCR corruption 'balf-blood' preserved as the corpus holds it.
Added by the verifier. 15-1876/s36 checked verbatim.

added_provisions.reason: 15-1876/s27 is the express provision governing division where half-blood brothers and sisters take, and s.30 applies only 'Except when otherwise expressly provided'. The map used s.30 to divide the sibling half of Kasun's estate without testing s.27 first. The result is unchanged, because s.25 admits only the half-bloods related to Kasun through his deceased mother, so there is no father's-side share to set against the mother's-side share and no full sibling to take a preferential half; but the step needed corpus support. Added as a supporting provision on both questions with a 'qualifies' edge to PROV-M025-007.

Both gold answer conclusions cite s.26 of the Ordinance by number as the alternative outcome if no parent of Sarathi survived her, but the map carried no entry for it, so the citation was unanchored. Added as a background provision on both questions with a 'cross_references' edge from PROV-M025-006. The researcher's alternative reading is right on the text: s.26 gives the property to brothers and sisters 'whether of the whole or balf-blood [sic]', so on that footing Amal alone would take.

The statute_only classification of both questions rests on the proposition that the Ordinance is not silent and so s.36 never sends the question to Roman-Dutch law, which is not in the corpus. That proposition was argued in authority_requirement_reason with no provision entry behind it. Added as a background provision on both questions.

question_decisions.note: The pedigree is worked out entirely from Part III of the Ordinance and no claim depends on case law, so statute_only and proposed_gold stand. No indispensable provision was rejected or left unresolved. Four claims are marked disputed: CL-M025-Q01-007 (cited provision does not establish what it is cited for), CL-M025-Q01-010 (grantees of the Administrator's Conveyance are not in the record and the s.531 limb cited is the wrong one), and CL-M025-Q01-012 and CL-M025-Q01-013 (both depend on Namal Silva being Sarathi's father and surviving her, which the background never states). CL-M025-Q01-014, which records those open facts, is verified. Hop count of 4 confirmed.

The arithmetic was re-derived independently and agrees: Amal 5/16, Sunil 4/16, Lalith 4/16, Sena 2/16, Namal Silva 1/16, summing to the entirety. CL-M025-Q02-008 and CL-M025-Q02-009 are marked disputed because the last two fractions turn on the unstated assumption that a parent of Sarathi survived her; CL-M025-Q02-010, which states the assumption, is verified. The open point is one of fact, not of authority, so the question is not reclassified or reserved. Hop count of 4 confirmed.

disagreements.researcher_position: Namal Silva is the father of Sarathi and Amal and was living on 8 August 2018, so under s.25 he takes half of the non-spousal half of Sarathi's share (1/16 of the land) and Amal the other 1/16, giving Amal 5/16.
disagreements.verifier_position: The background says only that Kamala died 'leaving her second husband Namal Silva and two children namely Sarathi and Amal'. It does not state that Namal is their father, nor that he was alive in 2018. The researcher's reading is the natural one and the answer discloses the assumption, but it is an assumption: if no parent of Sarathi survived her, s.26 (PROV-M025-902) sends the whole non-spousal 1/8 to Amal, giving Amal 3/8 and Namal Silva nothing. Both questions' conclusions therefore rest on a fact outside the record.

disagreements.researcher_position: Thilak died in 2017 with 'no surviving spouse disclosed', so s.22 is not engaged and his 1/2 passes wholly to Sunil and Lalith under s.24.
disagreements.verifier_position: The background says Thilak 'was previously married to Sumana' and separately that he was Kamala's ex-husband. 'Previously married' is not the same as divorced or widowed, and the corpus holds no marriage or divorce legislation to resolve it. If Sumana was still his spouse at his death she would take 1/2 of his 1/2 under s.22 and Sunil and Lalith would take 1/8 each rather than 1/4. The researcher's reading is the better one, but the map did not record the point at all.

disagreements.researcher_position: Administrator's Conveyance No.6231 of 21 March 2014 gave effect to the devolution of Kasun's estate on Thilak, Sarathi and Amal.
disagreements.verifier_position: The background names the executant (Thilak, as Administrator) but not the grantees. Reading the conveyance as a distribution to the intestate heirs is the only reading consistent with the termination of the testamentary proceeding, but it is a reading, and Civil Procedure Code s.724B as quoted does not itself close the gap.

unsupported_claims: CL-M025-Q01-007 cites Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 for the proposition that Kamala Silva held no interest at her death having gifted the entirety. Section 2 says only that dispositions of immovable property must be by notarially attested writing; it says nothing about a donor being divested. The proposition is sound but rests on the background facts (BG-3, BG-4), not on the cited provision.

CL-M025-Q01-010 states that the devolution 'was carried into effect' by Administrator's Conveyance No.6231. The background does not name the grantees, and the s.531 limb cited, (1)(b)(ii), is the certificate-of-heirship route rather than the administration route the facts describe.

CL-M025-Q01-012, CL-M025-Q01-013, CL-M025-Q02-008 and CL-M025-Q02-009 all attribute a share to Namal Silva on the footing that he is Sarathi's father and survived her. Neither fact is in the background and neither is supported by a cited provision.

CL-M025-Q01-006 states s.30 without its opening qualification 'Except when otherwise expressly provided'. Not wrong on these facts, but incomplete as a statement of the rule; s.27 (PROV-M025-901) is the express provision the qualification points to.
temporal_issues: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 (PROV-M025-010): the corpus holds only the text as amended by Acts No. 30 of 2022 and No. 4 of 2024. The deeds in the chain were executed in 2011 and 2014, so the governing text is not in the corpus. The researcher flagged this and kept the provision as background, which is the right handling.

Civil Procedure Code s.531 (PROV-M025-011): corpus latest_change_year 1993, before the 2013 testamentary proceeding, so the text is applicable. s.724B (PROV-M025-012): latest_change_year 1977, applicable at the 2014 termination.

Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance: 'acts' shows no amendment act for 15-1876 in the corpus and none of ss.2, 3, 20 to 30 or 36 carries an amendment event, so the same text governed the deaths in 2011, 2013, 2017 and 2018 and is in force at the matter reference date of 2024-10. No later amendment was wrongly relied on and no earlier version is needed.
s.20 was checked as the temporal gate for Part III and is satisfied: every death is after the 1876 proclamation and every marriage in the chain post-dates it.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: s.27 (division in the case of half-brothers and sisters) was absent from the map although the answer divides a sibling half among half-bloods under s.30, whose opening words defer to any express provision. Added as PROV-M025-901; outcome unchanged.

The second sentence of s.25 (surviving parent takes the whole where no brother or sister is alive) was cut from the PROV-M025-006 excerpt. It is the exception that makes Thilak's share a half rather than the entirety.
s.26 was cited by number in both conclusions with no provision entry. Added as PROV-M025-902.
s.36 was the load-bearing step in the statute_only classification with no provision entry. Added as PROV-M025-903.

ss.28, 29, 31, 32 and 33 were checked and are not engaged: a parent survives at each of the three intestacies except on the alternative footing for Sarathi, where s.26 disposes of the estate before ss.28 to 32 are reached, and no party is stated to be illegitimate.
The s.3 definition of 'unmarried' is correctly identified but the corpus excerpt cannot show which term it defines; corroborated by 'defs 15-1876 unmarried'.
case_law_dependence: None found. Both answers are worked out from Part III of the Ordinance and neither names a case, a report series or a common-law doctrine. s.36 is the only door to Roman-Dutch law and it opens only where the Ordinance is silent, which it is not on any step in this chain.

The one place where the corpus cannot support the answer is the conclusive effect of the partition decree of 25 October 2010, the Partition Law No. 21 of 1977 being absent from the corpus. The allotment to Gamini Jayasinghe is taken as a given fact, which keeps the gap out of the reasoning.
enrichment_issues: None. Both questions are classified 'keep' in the candidate file and enrichment.applied is false on both, with original_background carried and no added facts. No statute name, section number or conclusion is leaked into any background text.
duplicate_or_leak_issues: M025-Q01 and M025-Q02 share the same background and the same provision set, which is expected: Q02 is the arithmetic on the fractions Q01 establishes. The two gold answers are not duplicates - Q01 states the chain of instruments and devolutions, Q02 states the fractions - but a lawyer should confirm that scoring Q02 independently is meaningful when its answer is contained in Q01's conclusion.
Provision role sets are disjoint on both questions after the additions, and no provision is unused.

lawyer_questions: Decisive: is Namal Silva the father of Sarathi and Amal, and was he living on 8 August 2018? On the researcher's footing the shares are Amal 5/16, Sunil 1/4, Lalith 1/4, Sena 1/8, Namal Silva 1/16; if no parent of Sarathi survived her, s.26 gives Amal 3/8 and Namal Silva nothing. This is the only open fact that moves a share, and both questions' conclusions turn on it.

Does 'Thilak was previously married to Sumana' mean the marriage had ended before his death in 2017? If Sumana survived him as his spouse, s.22 would give her half of his half and Sunil and Lalith would take 1/8 each instead of 1/4.
Is it right to read Administrator's Conveyance No.6231 as a distribution to Kasun's intestate heirs when the background does not name the grantees?

Does the exclusion of Sunil and Lalith from Kasun's estate under the words 'by the side of the deceased parent' in s.25 accord with practice, given that they are half-blood siblings on the surviving parent's side?

The background calls Kasun Kamala's 'only son' but also names Sarathi and Amal as her two children, and the answer treats Amal as male. Nothing legal turns on it under s.25, which speaks of brothers and sisters alike, but the lawyer may want the pedigree drawn with Amal's sex settled.
Should Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 be cited at all when the corpus holds only the 2022/2024 text and the deeds are of 2011 and 2014?
